questions.question: Which of the following metals is generally considered the most reactive among the options provided, readily reacting with cold water?

options.explanation: Copper is a less reactive metal and does not react with cold water.
Gold is a noble metal and does not react with cold water.
Sodium is highly reactive and reacts vigorously with cold water.
Iron reacts with steam but not with cold water.

questions.explanation: Sodium is a highly reactive metal placed high in the reactivity series. It reacts vigorously with cold water, unlike copper, gold, or iron, which are less reactive.

options.explanation: Sodium is more electropositive, meaning it loses electrons more easily, leading to a vigorous reaction with water.

options.text: Iron is a liquid at room temperature.
options.explanation: Iron is a solid at room temperature and does not react with cold water.

options.text: Sodium forms a protective oxide layer.
options.explanation: Sodium does not form a protective oxide layer; it reacts immediately with water.

questions.explanation: Sodium is placed higher in the reactivity series than iron, making it more reactive. Sodium loses electrons more easily, leading to a vigorous reaction with water, whereas iron reacts slowly or only with steam.

questions.question: Which of the following metals will NOT react with dilute hydrochloric acid to produce hydrogen gas?

questions.explanation: A displacement reaction occurs when a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its salt solution. In Test tube X (Zinc sulphate + Iron): Iron is less reactive than zinc, so no reaction will occur. In Test tube Y (Copper sulphate + Iron): Iron is more reactive than copper, so iron will displace copper. In Test tube Z (Iron sulphate + Iron): No reaction will occur as iron cannot displace itself. Therefore, a displacement reaction will only occur in Test tube Y.
questions.hint: Compare the reactivity of iron with the metals in the salt solutions.
